memory_update.text: PWR should remain the reference leader for the grid-services/interconnection node, but not dominate the underfollowed discovery lane.

MYRG is a high-priority underfollowed candidate because transmission, distribution, and substation electrical construction are core disclosed activities and T&D represented a large portion of 2025 revenue.

NVEE is a service-layer hypothesis for utility engineering, substation design, geospatial inspection, asset management, and testing/certification; later layers must verify whether grid-related services are financially material.

This pass did not include Primoris Services, MasTec, Sterling Infrastructure, AECOM, Jacobs, or utility transmission asset owners; they should be screened in adjacent passes for power-delivery backlog, regulated transmission assets, permitting exposure, and data-center interconnection work.

The most important falsification test is whether project delays and margin pressure are driven by labor, permitting, engineering, and utility coordination constraints rather than equipment shortages alone.

node: Transmission construction, substation EPC, interconnection services, permitting, testing, and commissioning
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the grid-services/interconnection node identifies one reference leader and two underfollowed direct-exposure candidates. The node is service-heavy: high-voltage field labor, transmission/substation construction, engineering/design, utility coordination, testing/inspection, and commissioning can bottleneck grid expansion even when generation and electrical equipment are available. This pass avoids hyperscalers and equipment mega-caps and focuses on public companies whose reported services map directly to transmission, substation, utility design, EPC, inspection, and grid-reliability work.
